book.title: The Telegraph All New Cryptic Crosswords 4

clue.text: Vote against a celebration

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read as three words
second meaning: a lively party or spree, in British slang

explanation.walkthrough: The first half only works split up as BE A NO: someone who votes against becomes one of the noes. A beano is informal British English for a jolly party or outing.
explanation.definitionFit: A beano is a slang word for a noisy, festive party; read as be-a-no it describes casting a vote of opposition.

clue.text: Right to support monarch

parts.note: to prop is to hold up or support
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the cipher of the Queen

explanation.surface: It sounds like a citizen's entitlement to back the Crown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right to' looks like a phrase about entitlement; 'Right' is the definition on its own and 'to support' is one piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper means correct or fitting, so it is a synonym of right as an adjective.

clue.text: Lays on parties

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to lay on is to attack with blows, to beat
second meaning: big lively parties, in informal British usage

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lays on parties' reads as hosting them; but to lay on also means to beat someone, and a thrash is British slang for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrashes as a verb means beats, as a lay-on does, and as a plural noun means lavish parties.

clue.text: The sweet smell of anger?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a noun, the fragrant smoke of burning resins
second meaning: a verb, to make furious, stressed on the second syllable

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a noun phrase about anger's scent, but 'anger' is a verb here, a sense of the same word spoken with a different stress.
explanation.definitionFit: Incense is perfumed burnt material; to incense someone is to enrage them, so it means anger as a verb.

clue.text: One making predictions about a distant traveller

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the predictor's word wraps round what follows

parts.note: a seer is a prophet
taken as written
far means a long way off

explanation.surface: An astronomer forecasts the path of some far-off wanderer such as a comet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A distant traveller' looks like one phrase; 'a distant' goes inside the seer and 'traveller' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A seafarer is a sailor, someone who travels by sea.

clue.text: Cop in male form

indicators.note: to form is to shape, and these letters are shaped into a new word

parts.note: nine letters taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A cop of the male sex.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a fair description: a cop who is a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A policeman is an officer of the police who is a man, which is exactly a cop in male form.

clue.text: Close call when the gin ran out

indicators.note: the drinkers have run 'out' in disarray, so the letters before it are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: nine letters taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A narrow escape at a party: the gin almost ran dry.
explanation.walkthrough: The bar running out of gin is the picture; 'out' is what scrambles those three words into NEAR THING.
explanation.definitionFit: A near thing is an idiom for a narrow escape, something that almost went wrong.

clue.text: Live down under

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
down in spirits, or low in position

explanation.surface: It suggests living 'down under', in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down under' looks like one phrase meaning Australia, but 'down' belongs to the wordplay and 'under' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Below and under are synonyms as prepositions, both meaning beneath something.

clue.text: A speculator with his eye on target

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a stock-market investor who buys expecting prices to rise
second meaning: the centre of a dartboard or archery target is the eye named after this animal

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a trader focused on a goal; the second half is a cryptic hint at the bullseye at the centre of a target.
explanation.definitionFit: In markets a bull bets on rising prices, and the bullseye is the central ring of a target.

clue.text: Love to sleep longer than usual, no effort required

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
a nap is a short sleep
late means past the usual time

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys a long lie-in, as nothing needs doing.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a lazy morning; in fact love, sleep and 'longer than usual' are three separate pieces laid end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: Handed something on a plate is an idiom for getting it without having to work for it.

clue.text: Not just ugly

definitions.meaning: first meaning: lacking justice or fairness
second meaning: the opposite of fair in its old sense of beautiful

explanation.walkthrough: 'Not just ugly' reads as 'more than merely ugly'; the two halves are separate meanings, and the second relies on fair meaning beautiful.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfair means unjust, and since fair once meant beautiful, unfair can jokingly mean plain or ugly.

clue.text: Chief means of support

definitions.meaning: first meaning: principal, as in an archenemy or archbishop
second meaning: a curved structure that holds up a bridge or roof

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as 'the main source of income'; instead it is two meanings, an adjective and a structural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective arch means principal or leading; as a noun it is a curved structure bearing a load.

clue.text: Retired, alas, before new rise in pay

indicators.note: something that has retired has withdrawn or gone back, so this word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: taken as written, then turned around

indicators.note: a new version of a word is a remade one, so its letters are put in fresh order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A retired worker sighs, having just missed a pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rise in pay' looks like the definition, but 'rise' is fodder and only 'pay' defines; 'before' just orders the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Salaries are fixed regular payments to employees, so they are what an employer pays.

clue.text: Sneaky lob

definitions.meaning: first meaning: deceitful, done in secret

definitions.note: a noun; the answer here is an adjective describing such a throw, an underhand lob
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a throw delivered with the hand below the shoulder

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sneaky lob' reads as a crafty tennis shot; instead it is two senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Underhand means sly or secret, and also describes bowling or throwing with the arm kept low, as for a lob.

clue.text: The opposite of how prose should be written?

definitions.text: The opposite of how prose should be written?

parts.note: surface reading: a reversed or contrary thing, a mathematical term
setter's reading: prose is not poetry, so the opposite of how it is written is in metre and rhyme

explanation.surface: A puzzled thought about the proper way to write prose.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as IN VERSE: prose must not be written that way, so the opposite of prose style gives the phrase, which is also a word for opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Inverse is a formal synonym for opposite or reversed, and split in two it describes poetry.

clue.text: The height of distinction

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a raised piece of ground, a hill
second meaning: fame or high standing

explanation.walkthrough: 'The height of distinction' sounds like a single phrase for supreme excellence; it splits into a physical height and a social one.
explanation.definitionFit: An eminence is an elevation of land, and eminence also means renown or superiority of rank.

clue.text: Brown may start to fight, being tough

indicators.note: this says one piece comes at the beginning, ahead of the colour that follows it

parts.note: to spar is to box or fight
tan is a light brown colour

explanation.surface: Someone called Brown might pick a fight to prove how hard they are.
explanation.walkthrough: Brown looks like a person's name, but it is the colour; the clue puts the fighting word first and the colour after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Spartan describes austere, hardy living, after the famously disciplined ancient Spartans.

clue.text: One living on another camp for airborne troops?

parts.note: a para is a parachute soldier
a site is a place for setting up camp

explanation.surface: It suggests one base being stationed beside another, a camp for parachute troops.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the stretch: a paratroop base read as a para site.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasite is an organism that lives on or in a host, feeding off it.

clue.text: Fruity result of a naughty pair going to bed

indicators.note: a naughty word misbehaves, so its letters will not stay in line

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A cheeky couple go to bed, and something fruity follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruity' suggests something saucy, but the definition is a literal fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: An apricot is a soft orange stone fruit, so it is literally the product of a fruit tree.

clue.text: Permit one journey but don't check the speed

parts.note: to let is to allow
the Roman numeral for one
a trip is a journey

explanation.surface: Advice to a driver: allow one trip, but don't hold back on speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Let it rip is an idiom for going flat out with no restraint, so nothing is held back.

clue.text: Regret taking in son with deception

indicators.note: taking in means admitting inside, so the word for regret encloses the next piece

parts.note: to rue is to regret
S is the standard abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A parent regrets having been fooled by their son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking in' also means deceiving, which tempts it into the definition; here it only wraps one piece in another.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruse is a trick or stratagem meant to deceive.

clue.text: People of Derby, for instance

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a group sharing descent, a nation or folk
second meaning: the Derby is a famous English horse ... at Epsom

explanation.walkthrough: 'People of Derby' reads as the residents of the English city; the Derby is instead the horse race, an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A race is a people of common ancestry, and the Derby is an example of a race run by horses.

clue.text: Struggle for doctor getting into his overall

indicators.note: getting into means going inside, so the doctor goes within the garment

parts.note: a doctor's overall is a white coat
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A doctor fights to get into his work overalls.
explanation.walkthrough: MB is the British medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine. 'His' ties the overall to the doctor: a white coat.
explanation.definitionFit: Combat means fighting or conflict, and as a verb to struggle against.

clue.text: Figures will show how well they are working

definitions.text: Figures will show how well they are working

parts.note: surface reading: numbers, such as sales or performance statistics
setter's reading: body shapes reveal whether slimming regimes succeed

explanation.walkthrough: 'Figures' looks like statistics measuring workers' output; it is the shape of a body, which shows whether eating plans are succeeding.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's figure, their body shape, is the evidence that weight-loss regimes have worked.

clue.text: Eggs on toast

definitions.meaning: first meaning: encourages, shouts support for
second meaning: the word said when glasses are raised

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a breakfast order; 'eggs on' is the phrasal verb for urging someone forward.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheer someone is to urge them on, and cheers is what drinkers say when raising a toast.

clue.text: Why one can't drop off Simon in a storm

indicators.note: a storm throws everything about, so the letters it acts on are tossed into a new order

parts.note: eight letters taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Simon can't get to sleep because a storm is raging.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'in a' that seems to place Simon in the storm is part of the fodder; only 'storm' does the stirring.
explanation.definitionFit: Insomnia is the condition of being unable to sleep, which is the reason someone cannot drop off.

clue.text: It may be a touch unlucky for a batsman

definitions.text: It may be a touch unlucky for a batsman

parts.note: surface reading: a batsman who is slightly out of luck
setter's reading: a faint contact of ball on bat edge, which can lead to a catch and dismissal

explanation.surface: A cricketer suffers a small piece of bad luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A touch' looks like 'a little', qualifying 'unlucky'; in fact it is the noun, the faint glancing contact of bat and ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A snick is a light deflection off the edge of the bat in cricket, often the cause of a batsman being caught.

clue.text: Posse that is organised with all speed

indicators.note: to organise is to put in order, here a different order from the one the letters are given in

parts.note: nine letters taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A sheriff's posse gets itself together in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Posthaste is an adverb for very quickly, from the urgent riders of the old postal relay.
